Build Process

Running the build is as simple as npm run build. This will transpile the src into dist, copy any assets (e.g. the internal default configuration), and fix up the Short-form Paths.

Typescript configuration

Short-form Paths

In tsconfig.json the entry "paths" (see Paths) provides mappings from a shortened form to a longer form. Besides providing brevity these also account for arbitrary relative paths. So refering to @/constants will resolve to src/constants regardless of where the enclosing source file is in the src structure. This saves a lot of ‘’import constants from ‘../../../constants’`` along with having to maintain these relative paths if refactoring moves the file.

These paths are also used during testing (see :ref:)

Generally these are handled by tsc but when we want to run the transpiled .js files directly with node these paths cause a problem as they remain in their brief form. To avoid this, the Build Process runs tsc-alias (see tsc-alias) to post-process the transpiled files in dist, expanding the short forms into their corresponding long forms.

ts-node is used to provide developers with a simple way to run Typescript without needing to explicitly rebuild all the time. ts-node does not handle these short-form import references natively. We use tsconfig-paths/register (see tsconfig-paths) to handle processing these paths before they are executed. Use npm run dev to run pdt from src during development.
